editorial:
Imagine being stuck on a tiny metal platform two thousand feet in the air with no way down. That is exactly where you find Becky and Hunter, two best friends who love taking risks. They decide to climb a giant, rusty radio tower in the middle of nowhere to get over some personal trauma. The vibe is super intense from the start, and if you have a fear of heights, you will probably be gripping your seat the whole time. It is a simple story, but the feeling of being trapped in the open sky makes it feel like a nightmare you cannot wake up from.

What really works here is how the movie makes you feel the height. The acting is solid, and the tension builds up perfectly as they run out of water and hope. Some parts might feel a bit unrealistic, but it does not stop the excitement. You should definitely watch this if you love survival stories that make your palms sweat. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see every detail of the drop, or rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: You will find out that the whole survival struggle was actually a dream Becky had while she was unconscious. In reality, Hunter died early on when the ladder broke. Becky survives by using Hunter's body as a bridge to reach a lower platform and then uses a drone to call for help. She eventually gets rescued, and the movie ends with her finally finding peace after the scary experience.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves survival movies and high-stakes tension.
